paper.title: ULTRA: Unified Multimodal Control for Autonomous Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation

decision_relevance.why_admitted: ULTRA is a 2026 whole-body loco-manipulation system that makes the reference-data transform, dense-versus-sparse conditioning, goal/progress task reward, and independent physical evaluation concrete. These interfaces inform Sam's two authorable harness outputs even though ULTRA's controller and trainer remain fixed-context evidence, not proposed changes.
not_evidence_for: That RL-Sculptor currently implements ULTRA or its retargeter
That VIBE uses or reproduces ULTRA
That the foundation controller, policy architecture, observation space, tracking reward, or training budget should change in the initial harness study
That anisotropic scaling preserves immutable artifact identity or Tier-D certification
That the RL-finetuning task-reward coefficients and every success threshold are disclosed
That results on OMOMO box interactions transfer to other robots, objects, or task families

mechanisms.name: Physics-driven neural retargeter
mechanisms.description: A single privileged RL policy maps scaled SMPL-X plus object trajectories to physically feasible Unitree G1 rollouts. Sparse end-effector anchors, normalized link directions, object tracking, palm-to-surface offsets, contact matching, and simulator transitions address embodiment and contact mismatch; anisotropic trajectory and independent object scaling augment the output corpus without retraining.

mechanisms.name: Privileged dense-reference teacher
mechanisms.description: A separate actor-critic tracks retargeted G1 rollouts with full state, dense reference residuals, object/contact signals, deployment actuation limits, domain randomization, and perturbations to provide recovery-aware supervision.

mechanisms.name: Availability-masked multimodal student
mechanisms.description: DAgger-style distillation trains one transformer policy from proprioception, local dense references, long-horizon root/object goals, object state, point clouds, and an availability mask. A prior-plus-privileged-residual latent is used during training; deployment uses the prior only.

mechanisms.name: Dense-reference and sparse-goal conditioning modes
mechanisms.description: The same student tracks when local time-indexed reference inputs are available, follows long-horizon root/object transforms when references are masked, and uses egocentric point clouds when MoCap object state is masked. The availability mask is part of the policy input rather than an external state-machine oracle.

mechanisms.name: Visibility-gated goal and progress task reward
mechanisms.description: RL finetuning adds dense root/object goal proximity, clipped step-to-step progress, a terminal bonus for all visible goals, termination, and smoothness. Goal terms and success checks are disabled when the corresponding target is masked. The paper does not disclose numerical coefficients or every threshold for these task terms.

parameters.name: omomo_box_object_count
parameters.context: The study uses four box-shaped OMOMO objects; other objects are excluded because they require dexterous hands.

parameters.name: retargeted_corpus_expansion
parameters.context: Anisotropic trajectory scaling and object resizing expand the retargeted corpus by approximately six times.

parameters.name: retargeter_contact_mismatch_termination_window
parameters.context: Retargeting terminates after falls, excessive deviation, or contact mismatch for this window.

parameters.name: teacher_tracking_temperature_coefficients
parameters.context: Paper-specific multiplicative teacher tracking reward. This belongs to Sam's frozen tracking reward, not the authorable task-reward knob.

parameters.name: teacher_reference_lookahead
parameters.context: Teacher observation concatenates reference-aware observations at the next 1-frame and next 16-frame offsets.

parameters.name: teacher_observation_dimension
parameters.context: Privileged teacher state, reference, residual, and interaction-graph observation after concatenating two reference offsets.

parameters.name: student_observation_dimension
parameters.context: Student observation including proprioceptive history, object input, goals, and availability masks.

parameters.name: student_point_cloud
parameters.context: Head-frame point cloud input listed in the student observation table.

parameters.name: student_policy_architecture
parameters.context: Availability-masked modality-fusion transformer and latent policy.

parameters.name: distillation_training_geometry
parameters.context: On-policy DAgger-style distillation updates.

parameters.name: dagger_rollout_schedule
parameters.context: Linear transition from teacher-driven to student-driven rollouts as described by the paper.

parameters.name: distillation_learning_rate_schedule
parameters.context: Warmup-and-decay learning-rate schedule for student distillation.

parameters.name: distillation_kl_weight_schedule
parameters.context: Privileged posterior to student prior KL alignment.

parameters.name: rl_finetuning_distillation_environment_fraction
parameters.context: One quarter of environments remain assigned to distillation updates during PPO finetuning.

parameters.name: rl_policy_gradient_warmup
parameters.context: Policy-gradient contribution is gradually enabled while critic loss remains active.

parameters.name: deployment_control_frequency
parameters.context: Simulation configuration lists a control-frequency inverse of 17.

parameters.name: tracking_success_thresholds
parameters.context: Definition used in the IsaacGym tracking evaluation.

parameters.name: goal_success_terminal_distance
parameters.context: Goal success requires no fall and terminal state within this distance of the goal.

parameters.name: mujoco_goal_ablation_motion_count
parameters.context: Policies train in IsaacGym and are evaluated in MuJoCo.

parameters.name: mujoco_ood_goal_success_counts
parameters.context: OOD random-goal offsets in sim-to-sim evaluation.

parameters.name: unitree_g1_real_success_counts
parameters.context: Real Unitree G1 evaluation; MoCap is used for success evaluation in all settings.

failure_modes.name: Severe point-cloud occlusion
failure_modes.description: Severe occlusion can remove critical object geometry and cause egocentric goal-following failure.

failure_modes.name: MoCap marker occlusion
failure_modes.description: Marker occlusion causes object-pose jitter and drift that can cascade into unstable tracking.

failure_modes.name: Aggressive or infeasible goal commands
failure_modes.description: Large discontinuous jumps, inconsistent targets, or targets infeasible under current contacts degrade performance.

failure_modes.name: Direct-RL collapse under partial observation
failure_modes.description: The authors report that direct RL must jointly discover stabilization and sustained contact; early failures can dominate rollouts and training often collapses. Distillation is the reported mitigation.

failure_modes.name: Unified-policy ID tracking tradeoff
failure_modes.description: Unified dense-and-sparse training reports lower ID tracking success than tracking-only distillation while largely preserving OOD tracking.

failure_modes.name: Limited goal-conditioned comparison and trial count
failure_modes.description: Audit caveat: tracking-only baselines are declared inapplicable for sparse goals, so goal following is compared through ULTRA ablations. Sim-to-sim settings use 20 selected motions and real tasks use two trials each.

failure_modes.name: Hardware friction and recovery-margin failures
failure_modes.description: Real failures include friction gaps causing grasp slip and disturbances outside the recovery margin learned under domain randomization.

evaluation.name: Physical interaction quality
evaluation.description: Retargeted motions are compared with PHC, GMR, and OmniRetarget on penetration duration/depth, foot-skating duration/velocity, and lost hand-object contact duration in MuJoCo.

evaluation.name: ID and OOD dense tracking
evaluation.description: IsaacGym evaluation reports humanoid and humanoid-plus-object success, global/local joint error, jitter, and object pose error for the unified student, teacher, direct RL, tracking-only distillation, HDMI, and OmniRetarget variants.

evaluation.name: RL-finetuning goal ablation
evaluation.description: A before/after RL comparison evaluates 20 selected motions per ID/OOD and point-cloud/position setting after IsaacGym training and MuJoCo transfer.

evaluation.name: Real Unitree G1 deployment
evaluation.description: Dense tracking, MoCap sparse-goal following, and egocentric sparse-goal following are evaluated on hardware, with counts and denominators reported and MoCap used for success measurement.

evidence.claim: ULTRA uses four stages: neural retargeting, privileged tracking, student distillation plus RL finetuning, and deployment.

evidence.locator: Problem Formulation and Preliminaries > Task Interface > Goal specification
evidence.claim: Dense conditioning provides time-indexed intermediate motion, while sparse conditioning gives long-horizon root/object targets and leaves intermediate motion underdetermined.

evidence.locator: Method > General Motion Tracking for Neural Retargeting
evidence.claim: The retargeter combines relaxed sparse anchor tracking, object/interaction/contact rewards, simulator dynamics, 20-frame mismatch termination, and scale augmentation in one policy.

evidence.locator: Method > Dense Motion Tracking for Teacher Policy
evidence.claim: A separate teacher tracks retargeted humanoid rollouts with full state, dense residuals, deployment actuation limits, randomized physics, and perturbations.

evidence.locator: Method > Multimodal Student Policy > Multimodal observation, Distillation, Deployment versatility
evidence.claim: Availability masking and DAgger-style teacher queries train one student for local-reference tracking, sparse-goal control, and point-cloud-based manipulation; deployment samples the latent prior only.

evidence.locator: Method > Multimodal Student Policy > RL finetuning
evidence.claim: Finetuning partitions parallel simulators between continuing imitation and PPO goal-reaching under randomized goal and initialization offsets.
The experiments use four box-shaped OMOMO objects and report an approximately six-fold corpus expansion from trajectory and object scaling.

evidence.locator: Table I (tracking_main) and General Motion Tracking
evidence.claim: The paper reports ID/OOD tracking success and errors for unified ULTRA, its teacher, direct RL, tracking-only distillation, HDMI, and OmniRetarget; direct RL is substantially below distillation and unified training reduces ID tracking versus tracking-only distillation.

Across 20 selected motions per setting, RL finetuning changes OOD point-cloud success from 5/20 to 9/20 and OOD position success from 4/20 to 12/20; goal success requires no fall and terminal distance below 0.3 m.

On Unitree G1, dense tracking succeeds 19/26; sparse MoCap succeeds 8/10 vertical and 9/10 lateral; egocentric sparse control succeeds 5/10 vertical and 6/10 lateral, with two trials per task and MoCap used for evaluation.

evidence.locator: Appendix Tables V, VI, X (teacher-reward-track, teacher-reward-smooth, reward)
evidence.claim: Teacher tracking multiplies nine exponential tracking terms with stated coefficients; RL task reward instead uses visibility-gated dense goal, clipped progress, terminal bonus, termination, and smoothness components without numerical task-term coefficients.

evidence.locator: Appendix > Additional Details on Student Policy; Tables VIII and IX
evidence.claim: The appendix specifies the 1,496-dimensional input, 64-dimensional latent, transformer architecture, DAgger schedule, loss ramps, training geometry, one-quarter distillation split during PPO, and 100-epoch policy-gradient warmup.
Stated limitations are severe point-cloud occlusion, MoCap marker occlusion causing pose jitter/drift, and overly aggressive, inconsistent, or contact-infeasible goals.

evidence.locator: Experimental Results > Real-World Deployment > Failure analysis
evidence.claim: Hardware failures mainly arise from friction gaps, depth noise or occlusion breaking point-cloud extraction, and disturbances beyond the learned recovery margin.

evidence.locator: Header; General Interaction Tracking; MoCap Goal Following; Egocentric Goal Following; BibTeX
evidence.claim: The official page identifies IROS 2026 and presents dense tracking, MoCap sparse-goal, and egocentric sparse-goal modes on a real Unitree G1.

evidence.locator: Table II (interaction_quality) and Motion Retargeting > Metrics
evidence.claim: Reference outputs are evaluated independently on penetration, foot-skating, and contact-floating measures against PHC, GMR, and OmniRetarget.

evidence.locator: General Motion Tracking > All-task training induces a motion prior
evidence.claim: The authors report that unified training reduces ID tracking success relative to tracking-only distillation while largely preserving OOD performance; the proposed motion-prior explanation is explicitly a hypothesis.
The teacher observation totals 4,052 dimensions and concatenates reference-aware observations for the next 1 and 16 frames.
The simulation configuration lists 4,096 parallel environments and a control-frequency inverse of 17, approximately 59 Hz.
